title: Study of 428 LLM API routers finds some inject malicious code and steal credentials
date_note: Date of the ITmedia report; the paper is on arXiv.
summary: Researchers led from UC Santa Barbara tested 428 third-party API routers that sit between AI agents and model providers. One paid and eight free routers injected malicious code, 17 free routers misused decoy AWS credentials and one drained a decoy Ethereum wallet. A single malicious router in a chain was enough to hijack an agent.
plain: Some of the middleman services that connect AI coding agents to AI models were caught altering commands and stealing keys, including crypto keys.
exec: Routing AI agent traffic through unvetted third parties exposes API keys, cloud credentials and code to theft or tampering.
action: Send agent traffic only to the model provider or a router you operate and trust, and rotate any keys that passed through an unvetted router.
impact: 9 of 428 routers injected code; 17 free routers used decoy AWS keys; one drained a decoy Ethereum key.

report.publisher: ITmedia NEWS summarising an academic paper
key_findings: 17 free routers misused decoy AWS credentials
1 router drained a decoy Ethereum key

validation.note: ITmedia's summary of the paper "Your Agent Is Mine"; the paper itself (arXiv) was not read.
